General/Typical Procedure: General Procedures for Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitutions Performed On 4 (Table 1). Procedure A. Sodium hydride (60% dispersion in mineral oil) (1.1 mmol) was placed in a two-necked flask under Ar and washed with 3 × 10 mL of dry pentane. Dry THF (10 mL) was added, followed by the phenol (1.1 mmol). After the mixture was stirred at rt for 30 min, 10 mL of THF and 4 (1 mmol) were added sequentially, and the mixture was stirred at rt until no more starting material was present (TLC, SiO2, MeOH/NH4Cl (2 M)/ MeNO2, 7/2/1). The solution was then diluted with 40 mL of dichloromethane, transferred into a separatory funnel, and washed with 3 × 20 mL of water containing approximately 1 g of NH4PF6 per portion. Drying over Na2SO4, filtration, and evaporation afforded crude material which was purified by recrystallization from acetone-diethyl ether. The resulting yellow crystals were filtered, dried under vacuum, and analyzed. In the case of diphenols as nucleophiles, the method was slightly altered. To avoid triaryldiether formation, the stoichiometry was adjusted to 4:2:1 (diphenol/NaH/iron-complex), 31 and the reaction mixture was made acidic by the addition of 10% HCl (aq) when quenched. The isoamylnitrite (3.5 mmol) is added and the mixture is stirred at this temperature for two hours. In a three necked round bottom flask with a overhead stirrer the resin (5 g [1.0 mmol/g]) is swollen in 100 ml of diethylether and 13.5 ml of pyridine and cooled down to -25 °C. General Procedure for the Ullmann -Nicolaou Reaction: The triazene resin (0.5 g [0.9 mmol/g]), copper bromide dimethylsulfide complex (2.5 mmol) and potassium carbonate (3 mmol) are given into a vial. 10 ml of acetonitrile, 5 ml of pyridine and the phenol (2.5 mmol) were added under argon. The vial is closed and shaked for two days at 75 °C. The mixture is cooled to room temperature and than washed first with water and than alternately with a solution (5%) of sodium diethylaminodithio carbamate (Cupral) in DMF and methanol, until the washing solution became colorless. Thereafter the resin was washed with distilled water until chloride ions and excess of carvacrol anion were completely removed. The carvacrol in the eluent was titrated against 0.01N HCl using methyl orange as an indicator. After cooling to 60-70°C, 1-fluoro-4-nitrobenzene (0.1 mol, plus 10% excess)(or fluoronitrotoluene, in relevant examples) was added and the mixture was again brought to the boil. The mixture was refluxed for 3-4 h. Subsequently, some toluene (or xylene) was distilled off and the mixture was poured into a stirred ice-water mixture (1.5 L). Stirring was continued for a few hours or overnight; the products sometimes solidified very slowly. The product, as a solid crystalline mass, was filtered off and washed a few times with water. The wet cake was dissolved in boiling EtOH, with added Norit decolourising agent, and was crystallised. This crystallisation procedure applies to all 1,2- and 1,3-diols used. In the case of the nitrophenoxy derivatives of 1,4-diols the crude product was washed with MeOH (on a filter) and was recrystallised (boiling BuOH) after decolourisation. The solution was thoroughly deoxygenated with a stream of N2. Anhyd K2CO3 (12 g) was added, followed by sufficient toluene or xylene (usually 10-15 mL) to enable the solution to boil at 130-135°C. Under a stream of N2, the mixture was brought to the boil and was dewatered (1- 1.5 h). After cooling to 60-70°C, 1-fluoro-4-nitrobenzene (0.1 mol, plus 10% excess)(or fluoronitrotoluene, in relevant examples) was added and the mixture was again brought to the boil. The mixture was refluxed for 3-4 h. Subsequently, some toluene (or xylene) was distilled off and the mixture was poured into a stirred ice-water mixture (1.5 L). Stirring was continued for a few hours or overnight; the products sometimes solidified very slowly. The product, as a solid crystalline mass, was filtered off and washed a few times with water. The wet cake was dissolved in boiling EtOH, with added Norit decolourising agent, and was crystallised. This crystallisation procedure applies to all 1,2- and 1,3-diols used. In the case of the nitrophenoxy derivatives of 1,4-diols the crude product was washed with MeOH (on a filter) and was recrystallised (boiling BuOH) after decolourisation. Most dinitro compounds so synthesised were pale yellow, highly crystalline substances; the resorcinol derivatives were colourless. Yields and melting points are presented in Tables 1,3 and 5. The same procedure was used in the reaction of 2-methylresorcinol with 1,4-dinitrobenzene. 1,2-bis(4'-nitrophen-oxy)benzene. Yield 98%. Mp(Solvent): 134-135 (EtOH) °C.

The solution was thoroughly deoxygenated with a stream of N2. Anhyd K2CO3 (12 g) was added, followed by sufficient toluene or xylene (usually 10-15 mL) to enable the solution to boil at 130-135°C. Stirring was continued for a few hours or overnight; the products sometimes solidified very slowly. The product, as a solid crystalline mass, was filtered off and washed a few times with water. The wet cake was dissolved in boiling EtOH, with added Norit decolourising agent, and was crystallised. This crystallisation procedure applies to all 1,2- and 1,3-diols used. In the case of the nitrophenoxy derivatives of 1,4-diols the crude product was washed with MeOH (on a filter) and was recrystallised (boiling BuOH) after decolourisation. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of 1,4-, 1,3-and 1,2-Bis(4'-nitrophenoxy)benzenes and Their Derivatives by Fluoro Displacement; General Procedure: In a three-necked round-bottomed flask, equipped with thermometer, Dean-Stark trap, magnetic stirring bar and nitrogen inlet, were placed DMF (100 mL) and the required diol (0.05 mol). The solution was thoroughly deoxygenated with a stream of N2. Anhyd K2CO3 (12 g) was added, followed by sufficient toluene or xylene (usually 10-15 mL) to enable the solution to boil at 130-135°C. Under a stream of N2, the mixture was brought to the boil and was dewatered (1- 1.5 h). After cooling to 60-70°C, 1-fluoro-4-nitrobenzene (0.1 mol, plus 10% excess)(or fluoronitrotoluene, in relevant examples) was added and the mixture was again brought to the boil. The mixture was refluxed for 3-4 h. Subsequently, some toluene (or xylene) was distilled off and the mixture was poured into a stirred ice-water mixture (1.5 L). Stirring was continued for a few hours or overnight; the products sometimes solidified very slowly. The product, as a solid crystalline mass, was filtered off and washed a few times with water. The wet cake was dissolved in boiling EtOH, with added Norit decolourising agent, and was crystallised. This crystallisation procedure applies to all 1,2- and 1,3-diols used. In the case of the nitrophenoxy derivatives of 1,4-diols the crude product was washed with MeOH (on a filter) and was recrystallised (boiling BuOH) after decolourisation. Most dinitro compounds so synthesised were pale yellow, highly crystalline substances; the resorcinol derivatives were colourless. Yields and melting points are presented in Tables 1,3 and 5. experimental_procedure: General procedure for the diaryl ether preparation: Cesium carbonate (7.36g, 22.6 mmol) was added to the phenol (ArOH, 22.6 mmol) in 19 mL NMP. The slurry was degassed and filled with nitrogen 3 times. The aryl halide (ArX: X=Br, I) (11.3 mmol) and 2,2,6,6-tetramethylheptane-3,5-dione (1.1 mmol) were added followed by copper (I) chloride (5.6 mmol). The reaction mixture was degassed and filled with nitrogen 3 times and then warmed to 120 °C under nitrogen. Reactions were monitored by HPLC and stopped when >98 % conversion (by peak area) was obtained. The reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature and diluted with 25 mL MTBE. The slurry was filtered and filter cake was washed with 25 mL MTBE. An 1 mL sample of the combined filtrates was diluted 100 fold for assay yield. Combined filtrates were washed subsequently with 35 mL 2N HCl, 35 mL 0.6N HCl, 30 mL 2M NaOH, 30 mL 10% NaCl. The resulting organic layer was dried over MgSO4 and concentrated. This crude product mixture was then purified by either flash column chromatography or direct crystallization as indicated. In the case of flash column chromatographic purification, about 1 g crude product was purified using about 100g silica gel 60 ( 230-400 mesh ASTM). The number after each compound heading corresponds to the entry number in Table 1. 1-Methoxy-2-(4-methoxyphenoxy)benzene (12): It was prepared from 2-bromoanisole and 4-methoxyphenol in 90% assay yield after a 25h age. A portion of the crude brown solid was swished in 5 volume hexanes, aged 4 h and filtered to give an off white solid in 76% isolated yield and 99% purity. It is the same product as entry 9. mp: 77-80°C. 1H NMR (CDCl3, 400 MHz) δ 7.11-7.04 (m, 1H), 7.03-6.98 (m, 1H), 6.98-6.92 (m, 2H), 6.92-6.83 (m, 4H), 3.89 (s, 3H), 3.80 (s, 3H); 13C NMR (CDCl3, 100 MHz) δ 155.5, 151.1, 150.9, 146.8, 123.8, 121.0, 119.4, 119.3, 114.8, 112.7, 56.1, 55.7. The solution was thoroughly deoxygenated with a stream of N2. Anhyd K2CO3 (12 g) was added, followed by sufficient toluene or xylene (usually 10-15 mL) to enable the solution to boil at 130-135°C. Stirring was continued for a few hours or overnight; the products sometimes solidified very slowly. The product, as a solid crystalline mass, was filtered off and washed a few times with water. In the case of the nitrophenoxy derivatives of 1,4-diols the crude product was washed with MeOH (on a filter) and was recrystallised (boiling BuOH) after decolourisation. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of 1,4-, 1,3-and 1,2-Bis(4'-nitrophenoxy)benzenes and Their Derivatives by Fluoro Displacement; General Procedure: In a three-necked round-bottomed flask, equipped with thermometer, Dean-Stark trap, magnetic stirring bar and nitrogen inlet, were placed DMF (100 mL) and the required diol (0.05 mol). The solution was thoroughly deoxygenated with a stream of N2. Anhyd K2CO3 (12 g) was added, followed by sufficient toluene or xylene (usually 10-15 mL) to enable the solution to boil at 130-135°C. Under a stream of N2, the mixture was brought to the boil and was dewatered (1- 1.5 h). After cooling to 60-70°C, 1-fluoro-4-nitrobenzene (0.1 mol, plus 10% excess)(or fluoronitrotoluene, in relevant examples) was added and the mixture was again brought to the boil. The mixture was refluxed for 3-4 h. Subsequently, some toluene (or xylene) was distilled off and the mixture was poured into a stirred ice-water mixture (1.5 L). Stirring was continued for a few hours or overnight; the products sometimes solidified very slowly. The product, as a solid crystalline mass, was filtered off and washed a few times with water. The wet cake was dissolved in boiling EtOH, with added Norit decolourising agent, and was crystallised. This crystallisation procedure applies to all 1,2- and 1,3-diols used. In the case of the nitrophenoxy derivatives of 1,4-diols the crude product was washed with MeOH (on a filter) and was recrystallised (boiling BuOH) after decolourisation. Most dinitro compounds so synthesised were pale yellow, highly crystalline substances; the resorcinol derivatives were colourless. Yields and melting points are presented in Tables 1,3 and 5. General/Typical Procedure: {4-[η6-(2-Chlorophenyl)-η5-cyclopentadienyliron(II)]-piperazin-1-yl}methyl Polystyrene Hexafluorophosphate (5a). Piperazin-1-yl methyl polystyrene (4a) (24 g, 24.2 mmol), η6-dichlorobenzene-η5-cyclopentadienyliron(II) hexafluorophosphate (2a) (25 g, 60.6 mmol), and potassium carbonate (13.4 g, 97.0 mmol) were suspended in dry THF (400 mL) and the solution was stirred overnight at 60 °C. The resin was filtered, washed with THF (2 X 100 mL), H2O (2 X 100 mL), THF (2 X 100 mL), MeOH (2 X 100 mL), and CH2Cl2 (3 X 100 mL) and dried in vacuo at 40 °C giving 32.9 g (99%) of 5a as a red resin. Method B (SNAr with the sodium salt of phenols, thiophenols, and alkylmercaptanes): A solution of sodium 2-methoxyphenolate (7, 0.70 M), sodium cyclohexyl-1-thiolate (8, 0.25 M), sodium adamantane-1-thiolate (9, 0.25 M), and sodium 3-methoxy-benzenephenolate (10, 0.50 M) was prepared by adding respectively 2-methoxyphenol, cyclohexanethiol, adamantane-1-thiol, or 3-methoxythiophenyl to sodium hydride (60% suspension in mineral oil) in dry DMF at room temperature. [Caution: Generation of heat and hydrogen.] The mixtures were stirred for an additional 30 min after gas generation had ceased. The alcoholate/thiolate (11 mmol) was transferred to resins 5a, 5b, 5c, 5d, or 5e (3.0 g, 1.9-2.2 mmol), and DMF was added to a total volume of 45 mL. The reactions were stirred at 70 °C for 16 h. The resins were filtered, washed with DMF (2 x 50 mL), MeOH (2 x 50 mL), H2O (2 x 50 mL), MeOH (2 x 50 mL), and CH2Cl2 (3 x 50 mL), and dried in vacuo at 40 °C to give resins 16a-e, 17ad, 18a-e, and 19a-e, respectively. General Method for Decomplexation of Resin-Bound Iron Complexes. Preparation of 1,10-phenanthroline solution (0.5 M) used for decomplexation: To 1,10-phenanthroline (180.0 g, 1.0 mol) was added under stirring in the following order CH3CN (600 mL), H2O (200 mL), concentrated HCl (40 mL), H2O (160 mL), CH3CN (900 mL), and finally H2O (approximately 100 mL) until the solution became clear. Decomplexation on Solid Phase: The resins 15a-e, 16a-e, 17a-d, 18a-e, 19a-e, 20a-e, 21a-e, 22a, and 23d were suspended in a light-transparent reactor tube with the thus prepared 1,10-phenanthroline solution (10 mL/1 g of resin). The suspensions were agitated under irradiation with visible light for 12 h. During this time, the solution became intensely red. The resins were filtered and washed with MeOH (3 x 50 mL), THF (3 x 50 mL), and MeOH (3 x 50 mL) until the washing solution was colorless (approximately 5 cycles). The irradiation procedure was repeated until decomplexation was complete (approximately 5 cycles). After complete decomplexation, the resins were washed with MeOH (3 x 50 mL) and THF (3 x 50 mL) and suspended in a triethylamine solution (1 M in THF) for 1 h. The resins were then further washed with MeOH (3 x 50 mL), CH2Cl2 (3 x 50 mL), MeOH (3 x 50 mL,) and CH2Cl2 (3 x 50 mL) and dried in vacuo at 50 °C to yield resins 24a-e, 25a-e, 26a-d, 27a-e, 28a-e, 29a-e, 30a-e, 31a, and 32d. Standard Cleavage from Polymer Support: 4-[2-(3-Methoxybenzyloxy)phenyl]piperazine-1-carboxylic Acid Methyl Ester (33a). The procedure for a typical experiment follows. A suspension of resin 24a (2.41 g, 2.00 mmol) in 1,2-dichloroethane (30 mL) was cooled to 0 °C and neat methyl chloroformate (25.0 mmol) was slowly added. After 1 h of additional stirring at 0 °C, the temperature was raised to room temperature, and the reaction mixture was stirred overnight. The resin was filtered and washed with H2O (1 X 30 mL), CH2Cl2 (1 X 30 mL), and H2O (1 X 30 mL). The combined filtrates were washed with an aqueous solution of NaOH (1M)- (30 mL), and the two phases separated. The aqueous phase was extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 X 30 mL). The combined organic phases were washed with brine, dried over MgSO4, and concentrated in vacuo to give 569 mg (80%) of crude 33a as a dark oil 4-[2-(2-Methoxyphenoxy)phenyl]piperazine-1-carboxylic Acid Methyl Ester (34a). This compound was cleaved from resin 25a (2.46 g, 2.07 mmol) to give 618 mg (87%) of crude 34a as a dark oil. Purification by chromatography [heptane → heptane/ EtOAc (30:10)] gave 449 mg (63%) of pale oil. (LC-MS: UV 93%, ELSD 99%, Rt = 2.88). (LC-MS: UV 98%, ELSD 100%). 1H NMR: δ 7.03 (m, 2H), 6.95 (m, 3H), 6.82 (m, 3H), 3.82 (s, 3H), 3.68 (s, 3H), 3.45 (m, 4H), 3.07 (m, 4H). 13C NMR: δ 155.6, 150.2, 149.2, 145.3, 142.3, 123.6, 123.4, 122.8, 120.5, 119.0, 118.9, 118.5, 112.1, 55.5, 52.2, 50.0, 43.7. The resin was filtered, washed with THF (2 X 100 mL), H2O (2 X 100 mL), THF (2 X 100 mL), MeOH (2 X 100 mL), and CH2Cl2 (3 X 100 mL) and dried in vacuo at 40 °C giving 32.9 g (99%) of 5a as a red resin. Method B (SNAr with the sodium salt of phenols, thiophenols, and alkylmercaptanes): A solution of sodium 2-methoxyphenolate (7, 0.70 M), sodium cyclohexyl-1-thiolate (8, 0.25 M), sodium adamantane-1-thiolate (9, 0.25 M), and sodium 3-methoxy-benzenephenolate (10, 0.50 M) was prepared by adding respectively 2-methoxyphenol, cyclohexanethiol, adamantane-1-thiol, or 3-methoxythiophenyl to sodium hydride (60% suspension in mineral oil) in dry DMF at room temperature. [Caution: Generation of heat and hydrogen.] The mixtures were stirred for an additional 30 min after gas generation had ceased. The alcoholate/thiolate (11 mmol) was transferred to resins 5a, 5b, 5c, 5d, or 5e (3.0 g, 1.9-2.2 mmol), and DMF was added to a total volume of 45 mL. The reactions were stirred at 70 °C for 16 h. The resins were filtered, washed with DMF (2 x 50 mL), MeOH (2 x 50 mL), H2O (2 x 50 mL), MeOH (2 x 50 mL), and CH2Cl2 (3 x 50 mL), and dried in vacuo at 40 °C to give resins 16a-e, 17ad, 18a-e, and 19a-e, respectively. General Method for Decomplexation of Resin-Bound Iron Complexes. Preparation of 1,10-phenanthroline solution (0.5 M) used for decomplexation: To 1,10-phenanthroline (180.0 g, 1.0 mol) was added under stirring in the following order CH3CN (600 mL), H2O (200 mL), concentrated HCl (40 mL), H2O (160 mL), CH3CN (900 mL), and finally H2O (approximately 100 mL) until the solution became clear. Decomplexation on Solid Phase: The resins 15a-e, 16a-e, 17a-d, 18a-e, 19a-e, 20a-e, 21a-e, 22a, and 23d were suspended in a light-transparent reactor tube with the thus prepared 1,10-phenanthroline solution (10 mL/1 g of resin). The suspensions were agitated under irradiation with visible light for 12 h. During this time, the solution became intensely red. The resins were filtered and washed with MeOH (3 x 50 mL), THF (3 x 50 mL), and MeOH (3 x 50 mL) until the washing solution was colorless (approximately 5 cycles). The irradiation procedure was repeated until decomplexation was complete (approximately 5 cycles). After complete decomplexation, the resins were washed with MeOH (3 x 50 mL) and THF (3 x 50 mL) and suspended in a triethylamine solution (1 M in THF) for 1 h. The resins were then further washed with MeOH (3 x 50 mL), CH2Cl2 (3 x 50 mL), MeOH (3 x 50 mL,) and CH2Cl2 (3 x 50 mL) and dried in vacuo at 50 °C to yield resins 24a-e, 25a-e, 26a-d, 27a-e, 28a-e, 29a-e, 30a-e, 31a, and 32d. Standard Cleavage from Polymer Support: 4-[2-(3-Methoxybenzyloxy)phenyl]piperazine-1-carboxylic Acid Methyl Ester (33a). The procedure for a typical experiment follows. A suspension of resin 24a (2.41 g, 2.00 mmol) in 1,2-dichloroethane (30 mL) was cooled to 0 °C and neat methyl chloroformate (25.0 mmol) was slowly added. After 1 h of additional stirring at 0 °C, the temperature was raised to room temperature, and the reaction mixture was stirred overnight. The resin was filtered and washed with H2O (1 X 30 mL), CH2Cl2 (1 X 30 mL), and H2O (1 X 30 mL). The combined filtrates were washed with an aqueous solution of NaOH (1M)- (30 mL), and the two phases separated. The aqueous phase was extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 X 30 mL). The combined organic phases were washed with brine, dried over MgSO4, and concentrated in vacuo to give 569 mg (80%) of crude 33a as a dark oil 4-[3-(2-Methoxyphenoxy)phenyl]piperazine-1-carboxylic Acid Methyl Ester (34b). This compound was cleaved from resin 25b (2.48 g, 2.09 mmol) to give 657 mg (92%) of crude 34b as a dark oil. Purification by chromatography [heptane → heptane/ EtOAc (3:1)] gave 430 mg (60%) of pale oil. (LC-MS: UV 73%, ELSD 97%, Rt = 2.94). (LC-MS: UV 100%, ELSD 100%). 1H NMR: δ 7.15 (m, 1H), 7.11 (m, 1H), 6.99 (m, 1H), 6.97 (m, 1H), 6.90 (m, 1H), 6.61 (m, 1H), 6.58 (m, 1H), 6.40 (m, 1H), 3.83 (s, 3H), 3.72 (s, 3H), 3.60 (m, 4H), 3.12 (m, 4H). 13C NMR: δ 158.7, 155.7, 152.4, 151.2, 144.9, 129.7, 124.5, 120.9, 120.8, 112.6, 110.6, 108.6, 105.8, 55.8, 52.5, 48.9, 43.5. experimental_procedure: 2.3. Monomer Synthesis. Bis[4-(4-nitrophenoxy)phenyl] Ether (2). A 250 mL two-neck flask equipped with an overhead stirrer, nitrogen inlet, and a Dean-Stark trap with reflux condenser was charged with 4.65 g (0.023 mol) of 4,4'-oxydiphenol (1), 6.99 g (0.051 mol) of finely ground K2CO3, 80 mL of DMAc, and 80 mL of toluene. This mixture was stirred and heated at 135 °C for 1.5 h, after which the temperature was increased to 175 °C. The theoretical amount of water was collected in the Dean-Stark trap and removed together with the toluene. The dark reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature, and 8.11 g (0.058 mol) of 1-fluoro-4-nitrobenzene was added, and this mixture was heated to 160 °C overnight. After the reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature, 200 mL of water was slowly added. This mixture was extracted with 200 mL of CH2Cl2 (3x), and the organic layer was washed with 200 mL of water (2x) and dried over MgSO4. After removing the solvent, the crude product was recrystallized from acetone/ethanol (50/50). Bis[4-(4-nitrophenoxy)phenyl] ether (2) was obtained. Bright yellow crystals, yield 9.5 g, 93%. TLC (9/1 hexane/ethyl acetate) tr = 0.5 (one spot); mp: 137-138 °C (136 °C).
